title: M5 Restaurant Suite
tagline: From the first order to the last payslip.
music_mood: warm, upbeat, Friday-night energy that settles into confident calm

scenes.caption: Table 7: 41 minutes. Nobody knew.
scenes.problem: All forty seats are full and a table has waited forty-one minutes without anyone at the counter noticing.
scenes.narrator: Forty seats. One Friday in Makati. Table seven has waited forty-one minutes, and nobody knew.

character_lines.line: Ramon, table seven, forty-one minutes na. Hurry!

scenes.caption: Typed once. The kitchen can read it.
scenes.problem: The cook cannot read the waiter's handwriting, so orders come back wrong mid-rush.
scenes.narrator: Ramon takes table twelve on his phone: sisig, extra spicy, typed once, sent. The kitchen slip prints by the stove.

scenes.caption: Separate bills, two taps.
scenes.problem: A group wants separate bills, which on paper means re-adding everything on the back of a receipt.
scenes.narrator: Separate bills? Ramon moves the sinigang to its own tab. Both totals follow.

character_lines.line: Sino kay Kuya, sino kay Ate? Halo-halo, hati-hati.

scenes.caption: Senior 20%, logged for the BIR.
scenes.problem: A senior citizen discount done wrong is either an unhappy lola or a BIR finding; done by hand it is both a notebook and a prayer.
scenes.narrator: Lola at table twelve: twenty percent off, VAT exempt, name and ID in the senior book. A manager's PIN approves it.

character_lines.line: Lola, twenty percent po, walang VAT. Pangalan at OSCA ID lang.

scenes.caption: GCash, card, cash. No calculator.
scenes.problem: One bill, three ways to pay, six people in line, and a calculator on the counter.
scenes.narrator: One bill, three ways: GCash, card, cash. The change is on screen before the drawer opens.

character_lines.line: GCash, card, rest cash. Change, eleven twenty-five. Next!

scenes.caption: Count first. Then compare.
scenes.problem: At closing the drawer looks short and the cashier gets blamed for money she never touched.
scenes.narrator: Eleven PM. The drawer looks two-fifty short. Maria counts first, blind. Then the Z-reading shows what it expected.

scenes.caption: Sales up. Profit flat. Why?
scenes.problem: Sales are up but the bank balance is not, and the owner cannot see where the money leaks.
scenes.narrator: Monday. The dashboard: sales by day, by hour, by payment. And food cost, in one number.

character_lines.line: Thirty-two. Dati twenty-nine. Three percent of the month. Nasaan?

scenes.caption: Pork up ₱40 a kilo. Sisig price flat.
scenes.problem: The pork supplier raised prices and the best-selling sisig still sells at last year's price.
scenes.narrator: Pork up forty a kilo, sisig price flat. Every dish is a recipe, so the margin moves with the delivery.

character_lines.line: Green pa, twenty-eight. Limang piso ngayon, hindi fifty mamaya.

scenes.caption: Stock in, spoilage out, reorder in time.
scenes.problem: The garlic ran out mid-service on Friday and two kilos of kangkong wilted over the weekend, and nobody wrote any of it down.
scenes.narrator: Deliveries on credit go to what we owe. Staff meals and spoiled kangkong are logged. Stock on hand, with the reorder point.

scenes.caption: Books that close themselves.
scenes.problem: Month-end is a shoebox of receipts on the dining table and an accountant asking for the books.
scenes.narrator: Month-end used to be a shoebox. Now every sale and payout posts itself: income statement, balance sheet, who we owe.

character_lines.line: Bigas, fifteen days pa. Hindi ko na kailangang tandaan.

scenes.caption: Punches in. Hours out.
scenes.problem: The attendance lives on the fingerprint machine and payroll night means a calculator, a notebook and midnight.
scenes.narrator: The fifteenth. Punches come off the fingerprint machine: time in, time out, overtime, per person, per day.

scenes.caption: Payday before lunch, not midnight.
scenes.problem: Computing four salaries with overtime, cash advances and SSS by hand takes the whole evening and still gets argued over.
scenes.narrator: One payroll run: days times rate, overtime, advances deducted, SSS typed in. Post it. Payslips before lunch.

character_lines.line: Dati, hanggang midnight. Ngayon, bago mag-lunch.

scenes.caption: His payslip. His advance. His phone.
scenes.problem: Staff have to ask twice for a payslip and three times for their advance balance, and asking for an advance means a knock on the office door.
scenes.narrator: After shift, Ramon opens My Pay: net pay, every punch, his advance balance. He asks for fifteen hundred.

character_lines.line: Dati, tatambay ako sa labas ng office. Ngayon, phone lang.

scenes.caption: M5 Restaurant Suite
scenes.problem: The counter PC is six years old, there is no IT guy and no appetite for another monthly bill.
scenes.narrator: M5 Restaurant Suite. POS, inventory, books and payroll in one app, on the PC you already have.

character_lines.line: Anim na taon 'tong PC, walang IT guy. Forty seats. M5.
